THE CENSUS CLASS OF EVERY BUSINESS IN THE REGISTER (T-1006, of T-0988). The December 1835 State census counted the town BY CLASS — forty-four stores, eight taverns, twenty-two lawyers — and this register's `trade` field is free prose off the printed notice, 152 distinct strings for 206 businesses. There was no class to count. This file is the adjudication that supplies one, and it is ruled ONCE PER PRINTED TRADE STRING rather than per business, because the printed string is what is being read: two notices that print the same words are the same reading and must not be ruled apart. A business whose notice prints no trade at all is ruled by id, off the goods, in `business_overrides`.

THE PROSE IS NEVER REPLACED. `trade` stays verbatim in the gazetteer; the class is carried beside it as `trade_classes`, and tools/trade_census_1835.py sets the counts against the census. A business may hold more than one class — a store that is also a forwarding house is both, and the basis says so.

THE DATE IS THE WHOLE OF THE CAUTION and it belongs to the comparison, not here: the count was taken between 1 September and December 1835 and the scene is 1 July 1835. Nothing in this file is evidence that a business stood on the scene date.

boundaries.B1: `store` is a business that DEALS in goods it did not make, from a shop, store, warehouse or ware-room — or that prints the words store, merchant, merchandise or grocer.
boundaries.B2: A business that MAKES what it sells (tailor, baker, boot and shoe maker, cabinet maker, saddler, smith, carriage maker, soap and candle maker, hatter) or that sells a SERVICE (auction and commission, land agency, insurance, livery, surveying, lake carrying, dentistry) is `other`. The enumeration counts three services and no more: lawyers, physicians and schools.
boundaries.B3: A notice naming both making and dealing, or two enumerated classes, holds both.
boundaries.B4: A specialised line the census counts separately — books, drugs, jewellery and plate, tin and copper ware — takes that class instead of `store`. One such line among many in a general store's list does not.
boundaries.B5: THE RULING THAT MOVES THE BIGGEST NUMBER, stated so it can be disagreed with: the enumeration's parenthetical '(dry goods, hardware and groceries)' is read as a GLOSS on the majority and not as a restriction, so a boot-and-shoe store and a clothing store are counted among the forty-four.
boundaries.B6: A stall in a market, a sale out of a barn and a cargo sold off a vessel are not a store: the enumeration counts houses of business.

census_enumeration_note: T-0988's prose says sixteen classes; the paragraph as printed carries EIGHTEEN count-lines and all eighteen are enumerated above. Two of them — churches and schools — count structures rather than trades; the church row is not compared at all (T-0988 leaves the roofs to the roof programme) and the school row is compared under a stated caution.

register_cautions.detail: The register carries 'Noble & Wesencraft' and '[uncertain: Noble & Wesencaft]', both ruled `steam_saw_mill`. The second record's own id declares the reading uncertain. NO IDENTITY RULING IS MADE HERE — the class count reports both and names the pair, so a reader can see the double rather than have it hidden.

register_cautions.detail: Two St. Joseph steam saw mills and a Detroit hat house advertised in Chicago papers. The census counted the town; these are scoped `outside_town` and are counted apart from it.
